chunks: “Whoever purifies himself and then goes to his bed, he spends the night while his bed is like his masjid. If he remembers that he is not in a state of wudu (ablution), then let him perform tayammum from his covering, whatever it may be; and he continues to be in salat (prayer) so long as he remembers Allah, Mighty and Majestic.”

key_terms.تَطَهَّرَ: purified himself; entered a state of ritual purity
key_terms.دِثَارِهِ: his covering; the cloth or garment covering him
key_terms.صَلَاةٍ: salat (prayer); the state and reward of worship
key_terms.فَلْيَتَيَمَّمْ: let him perform tayammum; dry ablution as a substitute purification
key_terms.فِرَاشِهِ: his bed; the place where he lies down to sleep
key_terms.كَمَسْجِدِهِ: like his masjid; comparable to his place of prayer in merit
key_terms.وُضُوءٍ: wudu (ablution); the ritual state of purity before salat

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for sleeping in a state of wudu and remembering Allah before sleep?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the merit of going to sleep in a state of taharah (ritual purity) and keeping one's tongue and heart engaged in dhikr of Allah. It also indicates that if one remembers lacking wudu (ablution), tayammum with one's covering may be performed, and such remembrance keeps the person in the state and reward of salat (prayer).
